newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE provides regulatory blueprint to inquiry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE provides regulatory blueprint to inquiry.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) has submitted a market protection and efficiency blueprint to the Australian government's Wallis Inquiry.
The SFE said its submission is designed to harmonise existing regulatory regimes without sacrificing existing levels of consumer protection.
SFE chief executive said the plan demonstrates that it is not necessary to throw out all the safeguards in order to overcome rigidities in regulatory classifications.

"We recognise that completely separate regimes for capital raising, derivatives, foreign exchange, investment type insurance products and the like has created a small number of anomalies," Hoskins said.

"But completely merging all these separate regimes would create even further anomalies at a time Australia's financial markets should be devoting their energies to further enhancing our international competitiveness," he added.
Key elements of the blueprint are:-
*Common themes from existing product based regulatory regimes to be merge into core rules applying to a wide range of financial market acivity.
*More specific supplementary rules focusing on a narrow range of activities where necessary.
*Fewer licenses and authorisations needed to trade a range of converging financial products.
*Clearer focus on settlements risks and competitive neutrality in supervisory arrangements.
*Recognition that "one size fits all" approaches to financial market regulation would impede efficiency and ignore the need for similar activities to be separately regulated.
"The smarter way forward is to retain common elements in core rules without jettisoning other safeguards which have a narrower application," Hoskins added.
